archetypes.name: caller-inventory
archetypes.rationale: The plan deletes lib-larch-cache-touch.sh and slims .larch-keepalive fields; only repo evidence can confirm the plan's callsite enumeration is exhaustive and that no unlisted consumer silently breaks.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each artifact the plan deletes or renames (lib-larch-cache-touch.sh, the multi-field .larch-keepalive body, LARCH_UPGRADE_FALLBACK_SESSION_ROOTS, collect_active_session_versions, warn_preserved_active_version_once), verify that every callsite and reader in the file list — including agent-lint.toml allowlist rows, other skill scripts under skills/implement/, session-setup.md cross-references, and SKILL.md prose that names the deleted helpers — is present in the plan's change surface. Flag any file that the plan touches a dependency of but does not list for modification. Also check whether hook-stop-fail-close.sh, sessionstart-health.sh, or test-sessionstart-health.sh contain any read logic beyond the SESSION_ID field that the slim two-field .larch-keepalive shape would break. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: depth-alignment
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims maxdepth 4 reaches larch-logs/implement/<RUN_ID>/round-1/findings.md from the session root, but that path is at depth 5; a miscalibrated scan would silently misclassify active implement sessions as stale and delete them.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify whether the proposed cleanup newest-activity scan (find "$entry" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 4) correctly reaches every path the plan claims to protect, specifically larch-logs/implement/<RUN_ID>/manifest.json (depth 4 from session root) and larch-logs/implement/<RUN_ID>/round-1/findings.md (depth 5), by cross-referencing the actual directory-depth structure documented in docs/run-logs.md. Check whether the test-cleanup.sh cases for depth-3 run-log batches actually exercise the claimed depth boundary or merely test shallower paths. Also verify that the find loop and stat invocations in the proposed cleanup.sh are Bash 3.2 portable — no associative arrays, no readarray, no mapfile — and that any top-level grep probes in the new code use the command grep or subshell form required by BASH_AUTHORING.md §1 to avoid the wrapped-grep abort hazard. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
